terms.definition: A substance that produces hydrogen ions (H⁺) in aqueous solution.
A soluble base; produces hydroxide ions (OH⁻) in aqueous solution.
A substance that neutralises an acid, such as a metal oxide or hydroxide.
terms.examiner: Alkalis are bases that dissolve in water.

terms.definition: H⁺ + OH⁻ → H₂O: an acid reacts with a base to make a salt and water.
A compound formed when the hydrogen in an acid is replaced by a metal.
terms.examiner: Hydrochloric acid → chlorides; sulfuric acid → sulfates; nitric acid → nitrates.

terms.definition: Heating a solution to evaporate some water, then leaving it to cool so crystals form.
terms.examiner: Used to make a pure, dry soluble salt (required practical).
